Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 113, verse 1:

Surat al-Falaq is Madani [[Ibn al-Jawzi said in Zad al-Masir: 9/270, "There are two views on this. The first: it is Madani; this was narrated by Abu Salih from Ibn Abbas, and Qatadah and others held it. The second: it is Makki; this was narrated by Kurayb from Ibn Abbas, and al-Hasan, Ata', Ikrimah and Jabir held it. The first is more sound, and what supports it is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was bewitched while he was with Aisha, and then the two Mu'awwidhatayn were revealed to him."]] In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

* *

﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak.﴾ Ibn Abbas and Aisha, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: A boy from among the Jews used to serve the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Jews approached him and kept at him until he took some hair from the comb of the Prophet ﷺ and some teeth from his comb, and he gave them to the Jews, and they cast a spell on him with them. This was undertaken by Labid ibn al-A'sam, a man from the Jews, and so the two surahs were revealed concerning him. [[Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir: 4/575, from al-Tha'labi, then said: "He related it without an isnad, and it contains strangeness, and some of it is a severe oddity, while parts of it have supporting evidence from what has preceded, and Allah knows best."]]

Abu Hamid Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us: Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi informed us: Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Asamm related to us: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn [Abd al-Hakam] [[In "A" it is "Abd al-Hakim"; the correct form is what I have recorded.]] informed us: Anas ibn Iyad informed us, from [Hisham] [[In "A" it is "Hashim"; the correct form is what I have recorded.]], from his father, from Aisha, that the Prophet ﷺ was bewitched, to the extent that he imagined he had done something when he had not done it. He supplicated his Lord, then said: "Do you realise that Allah has given me a ruling on what I asked Him about?" Aisha said: "What is that, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Two men came to me; one sat at my head and the other at my feet. One of them said to his companion: 'What is the ailment of this man?' The other said: 'He is bewitched.' He asked: 'Who bewitched him?' He said: 'Labid ibn al-A'sam.' He asked: 'With what?' He said: 'With a comb, hair from a comb, and the sheath of a male date-spathe.' He asked: 'Where is it?' He said: 'In Dharwan,' and Dharwan is a well belonging to Banu Zuraiq." Aisha said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to it, then returned to Aisha and said: 'By Allah, its water is as if it were an infusion of henna, and its palm trees are as if they were the heads of devils.'" She said: I said to him: "O Messenger of Allah, why did you not bring it out?" He said: "As for me, Allah has cured me, and I disliked to stir up evil among the people because of it." [[Related by al-Bukhari in Bad' al-Khalq, chapter on the description of Iblis and his troops: 6/334; and Muslim in al-Salam, chapter on magic, no. (2189): 4/1719–1720; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 12/185–186.]]

It is also narrated that it was under a rock in the well; they lifted the rock and brought out the sheath of the spathe, and in it was the hair from his head and the teeth of his comb. [[Attributed by the author of al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/687 to Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il.]]

Al-Mutahhar ibn Ali al-Farisi informed us: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Salihani informed us: Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far Abu al-Shaykh al-Hafiz informed us: Ibn Abi Asim informed us: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah related to us: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from al-A'mash, from Yazid ibn Hayyan ibn Arqam, who said: A man from the Jews bewitched the Prophet ﷺ. He said: He was ailing from it for some days. He said: Jibril came to him and said: "A man from the Jews has bewitched you and tied knots for you [[Imam Ahmad added: "in the well of such-and-such," so he sent someone to fetch it.]]." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Ali, who extracted it and brought it, and whenever he undid a knot he found some relief, until the Messenger of Allah stood up as if he had been released from a fetter. He never mentioned that to the Jews, nor did they ever see it in his face. [[Related by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf: 7/30 (second section), and Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 4/367.]]

Muqatil and al-Kalbi said: it was on a string in which eleven knots had been tied. It was also said: the knots were pierced with a needle. So Allah revealed these two surahs, and they are eleven verses: Surat al-Falaq has five verses and Surat al-Nas has six verses. Every time a verse was recited, a knot was loosed, until all the knots were undone, and the Prophet ﷺ stood up as if he had been released from a fetter. [[Mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/687.]]

It is also narrated that he remained under its effect for six months, and it grew severe upon him for three nights, and then the two Mu'awwidhatayn were revealed.

Isma'il ibn Abd al-Qahir informed us: Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn Isa al-Juludi informed us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan related to us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj related to us: Bishr ibn Hilal al-Sawwaf related to us: [Abd al-Warith] [[He is Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id ibn Dhakwan al-Tamimi al-Anbari.]] related to us: Abd al-Aziz ibn Suhayb related to us, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id, that Jibril, peace be upon him, came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Muhammad, are you ailing?" He said: "Yes." He said: "In the name of Allah I recite over you, from everything that harms you, from the evil of every soul or envious eye; may Allah cure you. In the name of Allah I recite over you, and Allah cures you." [[Related by Muslim in the Book of al-Salam, chapter on medicine, sickness and incantations, no. (2186): 4/1718, except the last phrase ("and Allah cures you"), which is only in manuscript "A".]]

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of the daybreak.﴾ By "al-Falaq" is meant the dawn. This is the view of Jabir ibn Abd Allah, al-Hasan, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, Qatadah, and most of the exegetes. [[See: Ma'ani al-Quran of al-Farra': 3/301; Fath al-Bari: 8/741.]] It is also the narration of al-Awfi from Ibn Abbas, based on His saying "Splitter of the morning" (al-isbah).

It is narrated from Ibn Abbas that it is a prison in Hell. Al-Kalbi said: it is a valley in Hell.

Al-Dahhak said: it means creation in general, and this is the narration of al-Wali'i from Ibn Abbas. The first is the well-known view.

﴿From the evil of what He created, and from the evil of the darkness when it settles﴾ Abu al-Hasan al-Sarakhsi informed us. Zahir ibn Ahmad informed us. Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Mughallis informed us. Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us. Waki' narrated to us from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from [his maternal uncle] [[In "B" it reads Khalid ibn, and the correct reading is what I have established.]] al-Harith ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Salama, from A'isha, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) took my hand, looked at the moon, and said: "O A'isha, seek refuge in Allah from the evil of the darkness when it settles. This is the darkness when it settles." [[Recorded by al-Tirmidhi in Tafsir, Tafsir al-Mu'awwidhatayn, 9/302, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith." Also recorded by al-Nasa'i in 'Amal al-Yawm wa'l-Layla, p. 271, no. 305; al-Hakim, 2/541; Imam Ahmad, 6/61, 215; Abu Ya'la in al-Musnad, 4/272; al-Tabari, 30/352; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna, 5/167. Ibn Hajar added its attribution in al-Kafi al-Shaf, p. 190, to Ishaq and Ibn Abi Shayba, and graded it hasan in al-Fath, 8/741.]]

Accordingly, the meaning of it is: the moon when it eclipses and turns dark. "Waqab" means it entered into eclipse and began to disappear [and grew dark]. [[Missing in "B".]]

Ibn Abbas said: "al-ghasiq" is the night when its darkness comes from the east, enters everything, and makes it dark. "al-ghasaq" is darkness; it is said: ghasaq al-layl (غسق الليل) when it grew dark, [and aghsaq (أغسق)] [[In "A" it reads ightasaq (اغتسق).]]. This is also the saying of al-Hasan and Mujahid, meaning the night when it comes and enters. "al-wuqub" is entering, and it is the entry of the night by the setting of the sun.

Muqatil said: It means the darkness of the night when its blackness enters the light of the day.

It was also said: The night was called ghasiq because it is colder than the day, and al-ghasaq means coldness.

Ibn Zayd said: [meaning] [[Addition from "B".]] the Pleiades when they set. [[Ibn Jarir said (30/352-353): "The most correct of these sayings in my view is that it should be said: Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to seek refuge (from the evil of the ghasiq), which is that which becomes dark. It is said: ghasaq al-layl yaghsuq ghusuqan, when it grows dark. (When it waqab) means when it enters its darkness. The night when it enters its darkness is ghasiq, the star when it sets is ghasiq, and the moon when it waqab is ghasiq. He did not restrict it to some of these, but generalized the command, so that every ghasiq is included, since he (ﷺ) was commanded to seek refuge from its evil when it waqab."]] It is also said that diseases become more numerous at its setting and are lifted at its rising. [[See our commentary on the explanation of the hadith "When the star rises, the plague is lifted" in Hujjat Allah al-Baligha by al-Dihlawi (under print); Mushkil al-Athar by al-Tahawi, 3/92.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 113, verses 4–5:

﴿And from the evil of those who blow on knots,﴾ meaning the sorceresses who blow into the knots of the thread while reciting incantations over them. Abu Ubayda said: They are the daughters of Labid ibn al-A'sam, who bewitched the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿And from the evil of an envier when he envies,﴾ meaning [the Jews] [[Omitted from "A".]], for they used to envy the Prophet (ﷺ).
